impact:
Found 2026-08-05 while repairing ISS-073, which is its sibling one clause over in the same acceptanceAdditions entry. Unrecorded until now.

WHAT IS WRONG. .story/tickets/T-011.json acceptanceAdditions.storeIntegration clause (4) said T-011 "must inspect three fields, each a hard stop", listing reset.failed alongside reset.stoppedAtManifest and reset.stoppedOnAuthorityLoss. The latter two ARE booleans (src/snapshot/store.ts:1199, :1204). reset.failed is not: it is `failed: string[]` (store.ts:1197), documented as "Paths this reset could not remove. The next start retries; nothing is chased here."

An implementer following the binding ticket text writes `if (reset.failed) { /* hard stop */ }`. In JavaScript an EMPTY ARRAY IS TRUTHY. So the branch fires on every reset, including a completely clean one. The bootstrap then never rebuilds, and AC 1 — "a new generation is published" — fails on a healthy store.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY BUG. It has no failure signature that names its cause: no type error (the ticket is prose), no runtime error, no exception. The store resets correctly, reports success correctly, and the service simply declines to rebuild. A test named for the hard-stop behaviour PASSES, because the hard stop does fire; what no test observes is that it also fires when it must not. That is the same shape as ISS-073, whose wrong field name produced a branch that NEVER fires — this one produces a branch that ALWAYS fires. SIBLING CLAUSES of the same acceptanceAdditions.storeIntegration entry (ISS-073 is clause (6), this is clause (4)), opposite failure, both invisible.

The two are the project's class-(a) defect (a class fixed at one site and not its siblings): ISS-073 was filed against clause (6) and the identical species of error sat unexamined in clause (4).

The governing plan already had it right — docs/t011-headless-service-plan.md:460 says "reset.failed non-empty" — so this was drift between the plan and the ticket, in the direction that matters, since the ticket is what an implementer works from day to day.
resolution:
Resolved 2026-08-05 in the same edit that discovered it. Filed rather than fixed silently because the DEFECT PATTERN is worth more than the fix: this project's two recurring classes both appear in it, and the sibling clause had already been filed as ISS-073 without anyone checking clause (4).

THE FIX. acceptanceAdditions.storeIntegration clause (4) now reads: "reset.failed is a string[] (store.ts:1197) and must be tested for NON-EMPTINESS — `if (reset.failed.length > 0)`, never `if (reset.failed)`, because an empty array is truthy in JavaScript and a bare truthiness test halts the bootstrap on every CLEAN reset, so the store is never rebuilt and AC 1 fails for a reason no test name would give."

The rule is stated rather than just the corrected symbol, so the next reader learns why the shape matters instead of copying a token.

TEST OBLIGATION ADDED, because the original defect's whole danger was that it is unobservable from the outside: clause (6)'s required-test list now includes "a clean reset (failed === []) is followed by a rebuild rather than halting". Without that row the suite can be green while the service silently declines to rebuild — a test that cannot fail for the reason its name gives, which is this project's central standard (ISS-079/080).

VERIFIED, not assumed: src/snapshot/store.ts:1197 is `failed: string[];`; :1199 stoppedOnAuthorityLoss and :1204 stoppedAtManifest are the two real booleans; docs/t011-headless-service-plan.md:460 already said "reset.failed non-empty", confirming this was ticket-versus-plan drift rather than a design question.
title: T-011 acceptanceAdditions treats reset.failed as a boolean hard stop, but it is a string[] whose empty array is truthy — as written it halts the bootstrap on every clean reset
